gloss: to drink up; to drink it all

definitions.gloss: to drink up completely; to drink the last of
definitions.explanation: To drink something until none is left. The compound suffix {尽|つ}くす adds the sense of doing the action completely, to exhaustion or until nothing remains.

examples.japanese: ビールを{飲|の}み{尽|つ}くした。
examples.english: We drank up all the beer.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}らは{店|みせ}のワインを{飲|の}み{尽|つ}くした。
examples.english: They drank the bar's wine dry.

examples.japanese: {祝|いわ}いの{席|せき}で、{用意|ようい}した{酒|さけ}をみんなで{飲|の}み{尽|つ}くした。
examples.english: At the celebration, everyone drank up all the sake that had been prepared.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY:
- Transitive ({他動詞|たどうし}): Xを{飲|の}み{尽|つ}くす.

Compound of {飲|の}む (to drink) + {尽|つ}くす (to do exhaustively, use up).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {酒|さけ}を{飲|の}み{尽|つ}くす: to drink up all the alcohol
- {一滴|いってき}{残|のこ}らず{飲|の}み{尽|つ}くす: to drink up to the last drop

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {飲|の}み{干|ほ}す: to drink down; to drain — emptying a single container in one go, often a glass
- {使|つか}い{尽|つ}くす: to use up completely — the same {尽|つ}くす pattern with a different base verb
